name: Sarnia, Ontario
note: Fishing locations for this city. Downloaded with the city's map, not bundled with the app. Derived from the records that used to sit in src/App.jsx - see tools/build-spots.mjs.

spots.name: Point Edward, below the Blue Water Bridge
spots.water: St. Clair River — head of the river
spots.blurb: Where Lake Huron becomes the St. Clair River. Fast, cold and deep close in; the best known shore stretch in the area runs from the water treatment plant down to the bridge.
spots.hazards: The strongest current in this app. The head of the St. Clair runs hard and cold straight out of Lake Huron, and it is not a wading river. Stay on the bank.
spots.tip: The stretch from the water treatment plant down to the bridge is the known shore run. Heavy enough weight to hold bottom is the whole game.

spots.name: Centennial Park & Sarnia Bay
spots.blurb: City waterfront park along the bay, sheltered from the main current. Paved paths and open shoreline through the middle of town.
spots.hazards: Sheltered compared with the river, but still a working waterfront with boat traffic.
spots.tip: The bay is slower and warmer than the main channel, which changes what is in it - more perch and pike, fewer walleye.

spots.name: Canatara Park
spots.water: Lake Huron shore, and Lake Chipican inside the park
spots.blurb: Free municipal park with Lake Huron beach on one side and a small inland lake on the other — two quite different fisheries a few minutes apart.
spots.hazards: Open Lake Huron beach: onshore wind builds surf quickly and rip currents form along this shore. Lake Chipican inside the park is calm by comparison.
spots.tip: Two fisheries a few minutes apart - big-lake shore on one side, a small warmwater lake on the other. Pick by the wind.

spots.name: Bright's Grove shoreline
spots.blurb: Quieter Lake Huron shoreline east of the city. Open water fishing from the beach, best when the wind is off the land.
spots.hazards: Exposed shoreline. A west wind makes it unfishable and dangerous rather than merely uncomfortable.
spots.tip: Best when the wind is off the land and the water goes clear. That is also when you need to fish further out.
